challenge.method: Ran the supplied JavaScript unchanged on both contiguous parts of each source. Compared the original bodies, the normalized bodies including the notice, and the publisher agreement alone against the full SPDX text. Replaced “License Grants” with “License Conditions” as a negative control. Compared the tag’s target type and SHA with the raw text URL.
challenge.results: byte_identical=false, normalized_with_notice=true, normalized_agreement_only=false, publisher_notice=true, spdx_notice=true, separator_count=1, altered_clause_equal=false. SPDX puts the version on a separate line, changes wrapping and indentation, uses typographic quotes and omits the separator. Removing the notice or changing the Section 2 heading broke the match. The tag target was a commit with the exact required SHA.

limitations: The crosswalk covers only the two pinned representations under the supplied normalization. The California notice applies by its own terms. Project applicability, approval classification and redistribution rights fall outside this finding.
